summary: Shunsho Manabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Tohoku University (~1960–1964). He taught Lori Meeks and held positions at Hosen Gakuen College (~1974–1999) and Shikoku University (~2007–2017).
Shunsho Terakawa studied at the University of Tokyo and specialized in Buddhist studies. He later served as an Emeritus Professor at Otani University (~1994–2000).

Shunsuke Tsurumi was a philosopher who studied at Middlesex School and Harvard University under Willard Van Orman Quine (~1939–1942). He later held posts at Kyoto University (~1949–1951), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1954–1960), and Doshisha University (~1960–1970).
Shuntaro Kondo completed his PhD at Ryukoku University in 2011, working in Buddhist studies and religious studies. In 2012, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Shuntarō Matsuyama, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji. He held lecturer posts at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, and Tama Art University, and was a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design.

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his D.Lit. from Bukkyo University in 1993. He also served on the faculty at Bukkyo University, attested as Associate Professor in 1996 and Professor in 2005.

Shuyu Kanaoka specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952) and earning a doctorate from Toyo University in 1962. He served as an associate professor at Toyo University from around 1961 to 1992.
Shuyu Sakurai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1940–1943). He later served at Komazawa University from around 1949 to 1987, where he was an emeritus professor.

Shwe Zan Aung was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon (~1888–1891). In 1895, he studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw.
Shōdō Yamagami studied at Kyoto University (~1962–1964) and worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from around 1971 to 2005.
Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1933–1936). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1964 to 1983.

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma. They also studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Sayadaw U Kundala, U Sajjanasara, and Sayadaw U Sasana.

Sibani Dasgupta was an Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and under Rajendra Chandra Hazra. She completed a doctorate degree at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under the supervision of Sushil Kumar De.

Sibraj Chetry works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah. He was attested as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College in 2012.

Siegfried Goldschmidt studied Indology and linguistics at Berlin, Leipzig, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D. 1867), under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He taught Heinrich Zimmer and was an assistant professor at the University of Strasbourg in 1881.

Siegfried Lienhard studied Indology at Vienna, Paris, and Stockholm. He held posts at Göttingen, Banaras Hindu University, Kiel, Stockholm University, and the Collège de France, and served as Secretary General of the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (~1979–1994).

Siglinde Dietz, a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD at the University of Bonn in 1980 under Michael Hahn. She taught Ryutaro Tsuchida and Andrey Klebanov, and held a post at the University of Göttingen.
Signe Cohen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was a student of Ludo Rocher. She holds a post as Professor at the University of Missouri.

Signe Howell studied at SOAS University of London (~1974–1977) and the University of Oxford (~1977–1980), working in religious studies and other fields. She became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1989 and taught Heidi Fjeld.

Silvio Vita studied at Naples "L'Orientale" and Princeton, specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He directed the Italian School of East Asian Studies (~1996–2008) and taught at Naples, Rome Sapienza, and Kyoto University of Foreign Studies.
